legacy.original_title: 1.1 - Define the puzzle generator and uniqueness contract
legacy.body:
## Summary

Define how Logic Grid puzzles are generated and how uniqueness is proven.

## Context

The repository describes a generator and solver but has no puzzle schema,
uniqueness rule, or reproducible generation contract.

## Expected outcome

- Puzzle schema: categories, items, clues, solution.
- Seeded, reproducible generation.
- Validity: every category has the same item count, clues are consistent.
- Uniqueness: exactly one solution.
- Fixture set for valid, invalid, and ambiguous puzzles.

## Out of scope

- Rendering the grid.
- Training a learned model.
- Difficulty tuning.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A puzzle schema is documented and versioned.
- [ ] A seed produces the same puzzle.
- [ ] Invalid puzzles are rejected with a reason.
- [ ] Uniqueness is proven by the solver.
- [ ] Ambiguous puzzles are rejected.
- [ ] At least five fixtures cover valid and invalid cases.
- [ ] Generator and solver share the validity check.

## Plan

- [ ] Write the schema and invariants.
- [ ] Define the seeded generator interface.
- [ ] Implement the validator.
- [ ] Add fixtures.

## Validation

- [ ] Same seed = same puzzle.
- [ ] A duplicate item is rejected.
- [ ] A puzzle with two solutions is rejected.
- [ ] Fixtures pass in CI.

## References

- Game contract: #3
- Shared contracts: ops/templates#32
- Tests: ops/templates#34
